Subject: Request: one-off sign-on + equity refresh for Ryan Hidalgo (L5 Data Infra)

Hi David / Karthik / Lauren —

Short version: LinqPay has a strong candidate for our open L5 Data Infrastructure role (Ryan Hidalgo). They are asking for a one-time out-of-band sign-on and a modest equity refresh to offset a competing offer from a big fintech. I ran the numbers with hiring and comp planning and we think a limited exception makes sense to secure the hire and avoid a months-long reopening of the search.

Proposed package (one-off exception):
- Base: $210,000 (within band)
- Sign-on: $25,000 (one-time cash)
- Equity refresh: 0.90% additional RSU grant (4-year, standard vest)
- Start date target: Mar 2, 2026

Why this is an exception:
- Candidate has deep infra + real-time event processing experience that maps to product priorities (payments pipelines).
- Competing offer is public-cloud infra role with a higher stock upside; candidate explicitly cited equity as a deciding factor.
- Reopening the search would delay a key payments reliability project by ~3 months (business impact).

Budget and approvals:
- We will absorb the sign-on from the recruiting budget for Q1; equity refresh will be charged to the platform hiring pool (headcount already approved for the role).
- Attached: offer summary PDF and comp grid highlighting the L5 band and proposed uplift.

Ask: Can we get a final approval (or a clear counter) by Thursday so we can get an offer out to Ryan and keep LinqPay engaged? If approved, I'll work with Lauren to route the DocuSign and let Zoe send candidate comms.

Thanks —
Marissa

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear summary. A couple quick clarifying Qs before I sign off:
1) Headcount / org: confirming this uses the L5 open headcount already approved for Platform (no additional FTE request)?
2) P&L / budget code: which cost center takes the sign-on charge for Q1? I want to ensure Finance has a path in the ledger — if it's recruiting, is there enough runway?
3) Equity mechanics: is the 0.90% an acceleration of an existing grant or an absolute add-on to the long-term grant queue? Need to be explicit for comp ops.

If you can reply with those quick details I'm happy to approve or give a specific redline. If Finance needs to weigh in, loop them in but try to keep it tight (this candidate is likely to accept quickly).

-David
